basis: Canonical Banking77 labels plus permitted train/validation and Week 1 error-analysis evidence; no official-test outcome was used for subset design.
synthetic_assumptions: All workflows and time windows are fictional research controls, not real banking rules.
A transfer is treated as a bank-to-bank transfer; a card payment is a merchant authorization; a cash withdrawal is an ATM event.
When wording omits the decisive state or rail, downstream systems should prefer clarification or escalation rather than infer facts.

intents.business_meaning: A submitted bank transfer remains in processing and has no terminal success or failure state.
explicit_exclusions: marked completed but recipient lacks funds
intents.distinguishing_rule: Use only when the transfer itself is still non-terminal; a completed transfer with missing recipient credit belongs to transfer_not_received_by_recipient.
intents.expected_support_workflow: Confirm the displayed state and synthetic waiting window, then escalate only after the pending threshold or a risk flag.

intents.business_meaning: A transfer attempt reached a technical or processing failure state after submission.
intents.distinguishing_rule: A failure is a terminal processing outcome; a decline is an explicit refusal and a pending transfer has no terminal outcome.
intents.expected_support_workflow: Confirm the failed state, avoid duplicate retries, apply the fictional retry rule, and escalate repeated failures.

intents.business_meaning: A bank transfer was explicitly refused before it entered normal processing.
intents.distinguishing_rule: The decisive signal is an explicit transfer refusal; merchant card declines remain declined_card_payment.
intents.expected_support_workflow: State that the fictional transfer was not accepted, request no sensitive details, and route repeated or unexplained refusals for review.

intents.business_meaning: The sender sees a completed transfer but the intended recipient reports no credit.
intents.distinguishing_rule: Requires a completed sender-side state plus missing recipient credit; without completion it is not this intent.
intents.expected_support_workflow: Verify only non-sensitive transfer references, follow the fictional recipient-delay policy, and escalate after the stated window.

intents.business_meaning: A merchant card authorization remains pending and has not posted, declined, or reversed.
intents.distinguishing_rule: The merchant card authorization is still open; a reversal requires an earlier completed or held amount being returned.
intents.expected_support_workflow: Explain the fictional authorization window, avoid promising release, and escalate only when the pending threshold is exceeded.

intents.business_meaning: A merchant card authorization was explicitly refused at the point of payment.
intents.distinguishing_rule: The payment rail is merchant card and the state is immediate refusal, not processing or reversal.
intents.expected_support_workflow: Offer fictional low-risk checks without exposing rule logic; repeated declines are routed to review.

intents.business_meaning: A card payment hold or posting was later reversed and the amount is expected to return under the fictional ledger process.
intents.distinguishing_rule: A prior authorization or posting must have been undone; decline has no accepted amount and pending has no reversal.
intents.expected_support_workflow: Confirm the reversal state, explain the fictional return window, and escalate only if ledger credit is absent after that window.

intents.business_meaning: An ATM withdrawal entry remains pending after an ATM interaction.
intents.distinguishing_rule: The rail is ATM cash and the state is pending; recognition disputes are high-risk even if the entry is pending.
intents.expected_support_workflow: Confirm whether the customer recognizes the ATM event, then apply the fictional pending window or security escalation.

intents.business_meaning: An ATM refused a recognized cash withdrawal request and no cash was dispensed.
intents.distinguishing_rule: The customer recognizes the ATM attempt and it was refused; an unknown ATM transaction is always the recognition-dispute intent.
intents.expected_support_workflow: Confirm no cash was dispensed, provide fictional safe checks, and escalate repeated declines or any account-security concern.

intents.business_meaning: The customer disputes knowledge of an ATM cash withdrawal.
intents.distinguishing_rule: Customer non-recognition is decisive and overrides transaction-state troubleshooting; treat as a high-risk security event.
intents.expected_support_workflow: Do not perform ordinary troubleshooting only; preserve safety, collect no secrets, and use the approved synthetic escalation path.
